summary: Gemini TOML mirror (.gemini/commands/session-closeout.toml) is absent from CLOSEOUT_MIRRORS — W1b drift undetectable.
evidence: The new parametrized test test_closeout_mirror_documents_w1b_reinforcement_step iterates CLOSEOUT_MIRRORS but that list covers only 4 markdown mirrors (.claude/, .github/, .opencode/, .agents/). The .gemini/commands/session-closeout.toml mirror is modified by the PR but has no corresponding parametrized assertion — W1b drift in it would not be caught.
recommended_action: Add a GEMINI_TOML_MIRROR constant pointing to .gemini/commands/session-closeout.toml and include it in the test_closeout_mirror_documents_w1b_reinforcement_step parametrization. Adapt the assertion to handle TOML syntax if needed.

summary: W1b docs show do_closeout.py --reinforce-episode as single-value but the flag accepts action="append" (repeatable).
evidence: do_closeout.py uses add_argument("--reinforce-episode", action="append") — the flag is repeatable. The W1b block shows it as a single invocation with one episode id. This does not cause incorrect behaviour for the common case but could mislead agents into thinking only one value is accepted, and it contradicts the "never increment the same prior episode more than once per session" guard which operates per-episode not per-invocation.
recommended_action: Clarify in the W1b block that --reinforce-episode is repeatable but should only be invoked once per session per episode. E.g., add a note: "(do_closeout.py --reinforce-episode is repeatable; per-session idempotency is enforced internally — never pass the same episode id twice in one invocation.)"

summary: test_closeout_mirror_documents_w1b_reinforcement_step assertion is too weak — "W1b" substring is insufficient to guard substantive content.
evidence: The test only checks "W1b" in text. A stray mention, a comment, or a section header with "W1b" anywhere in the file would pass. It does not verify the CLI code blocks (reinforcement_count.py, do_closeout.py), the guard conditions (never increment same episode), or the log line format are present.
recommended_action: Add additional assertions: also check for "reinforcement_count.py" and "--reinforce-episode" in the text, and for the log line format "W1b ✓" to confirm the substantive instruction content landed.

summary: "Run exactly one of" gives no guidance on which path to choose — reinforcement_count.py vs do_closeout.py --reinforce-episode.
evidence: The W1b block presents two equivalent invocations without explaining when to prefer each. In practice, do_closeout.py is the integrated closeout script and should be preferred when running inside /session-closeout; reinforcement_count.py is the standalone option. Without guidance an agent may flip between paths non-deterministically.
recommended_action: Add a selection note, e.g.: "Prefer do_closeout.py --reinforce-episode when already running /session-closeout. Use reinforcement_count.py as the standalone option when calling W1b independently."

summary: Idempotency enforcement for do_closeout.py --reinforce-episode is not described — agents cannot verify the per-session guard holds.
evidence: The guard "Never increment the same prior episode more than once per session" is stated as a rule but does not describe which mechanism enforces it for the do_closeout.py path. reinforcement_count.py uses reinforced_by_sessions for enforcement, but it is unclear if do_closeout.py calls the same function with the same idempotency check.
recommended_action: Add a note: "Both paths enforce per-session idempotency via reinforced_by_sessions in scripts/reinforcement_count.py — passing the same episode id and session id twice will no-op on the second call."

summary: do_closeout.py does not accept --session-id on CLI but side-by-side placement with reinforcement_count.py (which does) could mislead.
evidence: The two code blocks appear adjacent. reinforcement_count.py has --session-id <active-session-id> as a required flag; do_closeout.py does not (it reads session id from scope-gate.json internally). An agent reading quickly could apply --session-id to the do_closeout.py invocation.
recommended_action: Add a parenthetical after the do_closeout.py block: "(session id is read automatically from .azoth/scope-gate.json — do not pass --session-id)".

summary: --source defaults to "manual" in reinforcement_count.py argparse; docs hardcode --source closeout — omitting it produces different metadata.
evidence: scripts/reinforcement_count.py argparse default for --source is "manual". The W1b block specifies --source closeout, which is correct for closeout use. However, an agent that abbreviates or omits the flag would silently get source="manual" in the episode record, making reinforcement provenance ambiguous in episodes.jsonl.
recommended_action: Add a note: "--source closeout is required; omitting it will record source=manual (the argparse default), which is incorrect for W1b."
